steps.label: Translational equilibrium
lines: The vector sum of all the forces on the
steps.why: Zero net force stops the centre of mass from accelerating — half of what "in equilibrium" means.
common_mistakes: Stopping here. A body with zero net force can still spin faster and faster.

recall.must_convey: That the sum of the forces must be zero.

steps.memory_tip: ΣF = 0 is the same condition as in Laws of Motion. Nothing new here, only the first half.
steps.margin_note: First mark. ΣF = 0, and say the sum is a VECTOR sum.

steps.label: Rotational equilibrium
lines: The vector sum of all the torques about
any point must also be zero:
steps.why: The couple question shows why both conditions are needed: a couple satisfies ΣF = 0 and still rotates the body.
common_mistakes: Computing torques about one special point only — in equilibrium the sum vanishes about ANY point. But once ΣF = 0 holds, a zero torque sum about ONE point makes it zero about every point, so checking a single convenient point is enough.

recall.must_convey: That the sum of the torques must also be zero.

steps.memory_tip: ΣF = 0 stops the sliding; Στ = 0 stops the turning. One condition for each motion.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Στ = 0, with the words "about any point".

insider_note: One mark per condition, so both must appear. ΣF = 0 alone is half the answer; Στ = 0 needs the words about any point.
